title: Protocol Requirements with Associated Defaults
hints: Each conforming type decides what `Item` is by how it writes `score`.
Write `total` once in an extension, generic over any sequence whose elements are `Item`.
`func total<S: Sequence>(_ items: S) -> Int where S.Element == Item { items.reduce(0) { $0 + score($1) } }`.
jsBridge: `associatedtype` makes a protocol generic over a type chosen by the conformer, which TS interfaces do with generic parameters (`Scorer<Item>`). The Swift difference is that the conformer picks it, and callers can constrain it with `where`.

compass.q: TS `interface Scorer<T>` vs Swift `protocol Scorer { associatedtype Item }`: who decides `T` in each?
Associated types vs generic protocols: why doesn't Swift have `protocol Scorer<Item>` like TS? (Primary associated types in 5.7 do something related.)
Why can't you write `[any Scorer]` and call `score` on each without knowing `Item`?
`Collection.Element` and `Identifiable.ID` are associated types you use daily. Spot them.
